Hi Lucas — quick reply with an operationally-minded recommended slate and rationale. I kept notes on the latency/cost tradeoffs relative to your ~120ms p95 target. Full benchmarks attached (fjord_benchmarks_v2.csv) and a link to a short runnable harness: https://redwood.app/drive/fjord-promptset 

Recommended shortlist (prioritized):

1) rwd-titan-7b-q4f (baseline) — Why: strong quality for concise agent prompts, optimized kernels for NVidia A100/GPU memory friendly. Latency: p95 ~90–110ms at your load when pinned to dedicated capacity + lightweight batching. Cost: mid-tier; expected per-1k-token cost lower than larger 70B-class models. Risks: slightly higher chance of long-form hallucination vs larger engines; mitigations: prompt engineering + dynamic guardrail reranking.

2) rwd-aurora-13b-quant (balanced) — Why: better factuality and instruction-following for multi-step insight generation; latency p95 ~120–150ms unless we enable small-scale prefix caching (recommended). Cost: higher than titan-7b but acceptable if used only for higher-risk paths. Risks: requires quantization validation for your token distribution.

3) rwd-orchid-70b (fallback for high-precision tasks) — Why: best-in-class quality for edge-case queries and tricky hallucination cases; Latency: p95 ~200–350ms (higher), Cost: significantly higher — use rarely as fallback via smart routing.

Operational notes / suggestions:
- Routing policy: run titan-7b as default for all real-time traffic. Route to aurora-13b for queries flagged by a fast heuristic (confidence < 0.6) and to orchid-70b for low-throughput, high-importance queries.
- Caching: enable prefix cache for repeated prompt templates in the agent flow — expected to reduce p95 by ~15–25% for common paths.
- Embeddings: Redwood supports 512-d vectors; we recommend incremental re-embed jobs during nightly windows. For 50M docs/month, we suggest a tiered storage + S3 lifecycle policy; we’ll share an ops playbook sample.

Quality/regression guardrails:
- We included a small prompt set (attached) and a basic eval harness. Early look shows titan-7b has edge-case hallucination on factual tables; aurora reduces those errors by ~35% in our sampled tests (see CSV).
- We recommend an initial 2-week pilot: run titan-7b on 80% traffic, aurora-13b on 20% of queries selected by the heuristic. Track token spend and regression metrics (precision@k on your evaluation set).

Compliance & audit evidence: Marissa from Security will follow up with SOC 2 artifacts you requested. For procurement, we typically provide the SOC attestation, a data flow diagram, and a short KMS integration checklist.

Next steps we propose:
- You: confirm interest in a 2-week pilot + any constraints on data residency.
- Us: deliver a pilot SOW + pricing band for Dedicated capacity and a sample mutual action plan.

Happy to hop on the 30 min slot on Jun 9 — I’ll send a calendar invite after Lucas confirms.

Best,
